title: Pharma pays for platforms and validated targets
subtitle: Selected RNA-medicine deals, US$ millions, log scale. Acquisitions show headline equity value; licensing deals show upfront cash.

items.label: Merck buys Sirna (2006)
items.detail: Merck acquires RNAi company Sirna Therapeutics.

items.label: Alnylam buys Sirna from Merck (2014)
items.detail: During the 'RNAi winter', Merck exits RNAi and sells Sirna to Alnylam for about $175M upfront in cash and stock, plus milestones.

items.label: Novartis buys The Medicines Co. (2020)
items.detail: For inclisiran, a twice-yearly PCSK9 siRNA licensed from Alnylam.

items.label: BioNTech buys CureVac (2025)
items.detail: All-stock acquisition of an mRNA peer, announced June 2025.

items.label: Lilly buys Verve (2025)
items.detail: In vivo base editing of PCSK9 and other cardiovascular genes, delivered as mRNA in lipid nanoparticles. Includes a contingent value right.

items.label: Novartis buys Avidity (2025–26)
items.detail: Antibody–oligonucleotide conjugates that deliver RNA drugs to muscle. Announced October 2025, closed February 2026.

items.label: AstraZeneca–Ionis, eplontersen (2021)
items.detail: Upfront payment for rights to an antisense drug for transthyretin amyloidosis.

items.label: Roche–Alnylam, zilebesiran (2023)
items.detail: Upfront for a hypertension siRNA, with up to about $2.8B in total potential payments.
